ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle PQR. There is a right-angle mark at point Q, so \triangle PQR is a right triangle, and the hypotenuse is PR. Point S is located on PR. Segment QS connects from Q to PR, and there is a perpendicular mark at S, indicating that QS \perp PR, and it is the altitude from the right-angle vertex Q to the hypotenuse PR. The hypotenuse PR is divided by S into two segments: PS is labeled 2, and SR is labeled 4. The base PQ is labeled y. Reasoning: Because PR = PS + SR = 2 + 4 = 6. By the leg projection theorem of a right triangle, the square of the right leg PQ equals the product of the hypotenuse PR and its adjacent hypotenuse segment PS, that is, PQ^2 = PR \cdot PS. Therefore y^2 = 6 \cdot 2 = 12, so y = \sqrt{12} = 2\sqrt{3}.

method.method_draft: From the diagram, identify triangle PQR as a right triangle with the right angle at Q, and identify QS as an altitude from Q to the hypotenuse PR because QS is marked perpendicular to PR at S. Read the hypotenuse pieces from the image: PS = 2 and SR = 4, so PR = 6. Use the right-triangle leg projection theorem: the square of leg PQ equals the hypotenuse PR times the adjacent hypotenuse segment PS. Therefore y^2 = PQ^2 = PR · PS = 6 · 2 = 12, so y = sqrt(12) = 2sqrt(3).
